title: Maintain project participation and identity
summary: Register, inspect, move, pause, resume, retire, or seed a project while preserving stable identity, repository history, and activation cursors.
use_when: A folder should participate under an exact Semantics identity or its lifecycle should change.
Bootstrap vocabulary, activation coverage, move continuity, or retirement conditions must be understood.
do_not_use_when: Only maintained terminology should be read; use semantics.repository.explore.
Service installation, deployment, or intake retry is the subject; use the corresponding feature and project operation.
outcome: A selected durable project record or one atomic bootstrap revision with preserved identity and documented lifecycle boundaries.

interfaces.label: Project registry
interfaces.invocation: semantics project register ID ROOT; semantics project list; semantics project show ID

interfaces.label: Project lifecycle
interfaces.invocation: semantics project move ID NEW_ROOT; semantics project pause ID; semantics project resume ID; semantics project retire ID

interfaces.label: Bootstrap seed
interfaces.invocation: semantics repository seed PROJECT --label LABEL --meaning MEANING [--grounding STATEMENT]

effects: Registration stores the canonical folder and captures its current Annals watermark, excluding earlier documents.
Move appends path history; pause fences late commits; resume revalidates the marker.
Permanent retirement closes only eligible unstarted intake atomically. Seed commits only at revision 0.
authority: Semantics owns stable project identity, path history, lifecycle, activation and scan cursors, and seed validation.
The project owns its participation marker and runtime behavior. Annals owns upstream library/feed identity and cursor meaning.
success: The selected project identity and canonical root match the exact marker, and the durable receipt reflects the intended lifecycle.
Seed returns one validated revision; moves preserve repository and both cursor histories.
failure_and_recovery: Invalid markers, roots, identities, lifecycle transitions, or seed validation refuse the transition.
Retirement refuses attempted, processing, failed, correlated, or awaiting-review intake without changing project or intake.
Unavailable watermark blocks registration; inspect exact project, HEAD, and retained work instead of inventing cursors or clearing correlations.
privacy: Project paths, source labels and digests, meanings, and retained intake remain private local state.
does_not_authorize: Model jobs, upstream mutation, direct SQLite access, disclosure, or retained-state deletion.

consumers.statement: Local contributors and typed CLI clients may inspect or maintain participating project folders through supported Semantics operations.

preconditions.statement: Registration and move require a canonical directory and exact marker in regular root AGENTS.md; seeding requires revision 0; retirement requires paused state and no blocking retained work.

inputs.statement: Inputs are a stable lowercase project ID, selected canonical root, intended lifecycle action, or one seed definition/project-local Markdown source.

outputs.statement: The semantics CLI prints plain text by default. --json selects the existing compact command-specific JSON schema and coded failures on stderr. The typed client and pinned worker explicitly request JSON; machine callers must pass --json. Output schemas, retained state, effects and exit statuses are unchanged.
Project list returns ID, canonical current path, lifecycle status, and HEAD. Project show and operation receipts return the complete selected record; seeding returns the committed bootstrap result.

data_semantics.statement: Registration activates at the current opaque Annals watermark, move preserves identity and separate cursor histories, pause rejects late commits, and retirement is permanent and retains history.

identity_and_units.statement: Stable project IDs survive path changes; concept IDs and revisions remain project-local; Annals and legacy cursor bytes are distinct and opaque.
No pricing or quantitative consumption unit is defined.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Project list covers registered project summaries; selected show/receipt describes the selected stored record. Registration coverage starts after its captured watermark rather than at the beginning of the feed.
No activation latency or registry capacity objective is promised.

access.statement: Local-user CLI and typed client operations use Semantics private state; registration reads one configured Annals decisions feed and seeding reads a project-local source.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Registry changes and seed commits are durable. Retirement and eligible intake closure are atomic, and refusal leaves all state unchanged. Path history is appended and separate cursor histories are preserved.

operational_limits.statement: Bootstrap seeding is allowed only at revision 0. Retirement cannot clear attempted, processing, failed, correlated, or awaiting-review work.
No registry capacity or wall-clock operation objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Stable identity, historical path/cursor records, and revision replay remain preserved; provider release, persistent schema, and contracts have independent versions.
No retention horizon or future migration/deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: Registration captures the current watermark and exact identity of the configured Annals decisions library.
Seed validation and repository identity use the supported local semantic effect/replay contract.
